claims.text: A machine-learning model combining atomic-scale disorder metrics and anharmonic lattice-dynamics parameters will predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional averaged-property models.
Configurational entropy and local strain fields are useful disorder-sensitive descriptors for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The target samples are near-equimolar, well-mixed, disordered solid-solution high-entropy alloys.
The proposed workflow couples DFT phonon calculations to supervised machine-learning regression.
The regression model will include disorder-sensitive descriptors and anharmonic interaction parameters.
The approach is intended for ambient to moderately elevated temperatures at which anharmonic effects and local-strain variations are appreciable.
Configurational disorder and local strain fields modulate phonon lifetimes through enhanced anharmonic scattering.
Explicitly accounting for structural disorder and anharmonic interactions enables the model to capture variations in phonon-scattering rates that conventional models average out.
Capturing variations in phonon-scattering rates will improve the accuracy of low-thermal-conductivity predictions.
The proposed model will improve phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy by approximately 15–20%.
The proposed model will successfully identify high-entropy alloys whose phonon thermal conductivity is below an application-specific insulation threshold.
The baseline models use averaged compositional parameters and simplified phonon-scattering treatments without disorder-sensitive or anharmonic descriptors.
Applicability is limited to compositional and structural-disorder regimes adequately represented by the selected descriptors.
Applicability may be limited to temperature regimes in which anharmonic effects dominate thermal transport.
Electron-phonon coupling and microstructural inhomogeneity may reduce the model's performance when they contribute significantly to thermal transport.
Experimental phonon thermal conductivity will be measured over a range of temperatures using methods such as time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-flash analysis.
Prediction errors from the hybrid and conventional models will be compared using statistical metrics such as RMSE.

The hypothesis is falsified if the hybrid approach fails to produce a statistically significant error reduction of at least 15% relative to the conventional model when identifying alloys below the conductivity threshold.
